item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a separator modified with oxygen-doped carbon nitride (CNOI) that pre-desolvates Na⁺ via polar N/O sites before interfacial charge transfer, enabling uniform Na⁺ flux and a thin, ion-conductive SEI. This yields 93.0% initial Coulombic efficiency, 297.7 mAh g⁻¹ after 600 cycles, excellent rate performance, and −40°C operation, establishing separator-driven pre-desolvation as a transferable interfacial engineering strategy for practical hard-carbon anodes.

item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using oxygen-rich carbon quantum dots (38.83 wt% O) that self-assemble into a 2D ion-transport network in ZnSO₄ electrolyte, enabling multiscale synergistic regulation: solvation-sheath reconstitution (desolvation barrier 23.6→17.8 kJ mol⁻¹), enhanced Zn²⁺ transference (0.51→0.85) and conductivity (40→93 mS cm⁻¹), and preferential Zn(002) deposition. Significance: ultralong life (>10 000 h), 99.6% efficiency, >96.1% capacity after 100 000 cycles, wide −10–60 °C operation, and self-healing.

item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in introducing low-valence Cs⁺ into NFPP to trigger charge compensation that pre-stabilizes Fe³⁺, creating a built-in electric field and electron-relaying states that lower the small-polaron hopping barrier. Hall-effect measurements directly validate enhanced carrier mobility and concentration without the usual doping trade-off. This enables ultrafast charging (80% in 7.9 min at 5 C; full charge in 58 s at 50 C), offering a design paradigm for conductive polyanionic cathodes.

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Non-stoichiometric tunnel-structured Mo5O14 enables reversible H3O+ intercalation without phase transition or lattice strain, overcoming proton-induced instability in aqueous proton batteries. It delivers 271 mAh g−1, ultrahigh-rate capability (300 A g−1), and 310,000-cycle stability, plus a full cell with 73.3 Wh kg−1 and flexible micro-cells, establishing phase-stable non-stoichiometric oxides as a design strategy for durable proton storage.
🏷 proton battery · molybdenum oxide · tunnel structure · H3O+ intercalation · phase stability

Advanced Energy Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This Review uniquely bridges ALD/MLD surface chemistry with process design for energy-storage interfaces, addressing complex real-world substrates beyond ideal oxides. Its chemistry–process–structure–function framework links precursor pathways and nucleation to ionic transport, kinetics, and mechanical stability across Li and beyond-Li systems, while assessing scalability and validation. Six design rules presented as a decision flow translate mechanistic insight into practical interface engineering guidance.

item.description:

Advanced Science | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in a formation-stage Fe interfacial regulation strategy that avoids bulk substitution, instead creating low-content, highly dispersed surface/interface Fe species that tune the local Mn─O environment and nanosheet growth. This improves Zn2+ kinetics and suppresses Mn dissolution while preserving Mn redox chemistry, enabling high capacity (409.29 mAh g−1) and durable cycling (81.1% retention after 3000 cycles), offering a design route for stable Mn-based aqueous Zn-ion cathodes.

Advanced Science | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in revealing that Zr in LiNiO₂ predominantly enriches at primary particle surfaces under oxygen-rich conditions, while oxygen-deficient synthesis stabilizes a cation-disordered Li₁₋ₓNi₁₊ₓO₂ phase promoting grain elongation. Significance: only 1–3% Zr suffices to boost cyclability via surface enrichment and low bulk doping, whereas excess Zr forms insulating Li₂ZrO₃, reducing capacity—guiding optimal doping design.

item.description:

Advanced Science | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in using fluorine-free methyl tert-butyl ether as a weakly coordinating diluent in THF/NaFSI to create a localized high-concentration electrolyte that shifts solvation from solvent-separated ion pairs to contact ion pairs/aggregates. This weak-solvation design accelerates desolvation, forms an inorganic-rich interphase, and enables fast-charging, dendrite-free sodium metal batteries with high-loading cathodes and PFAS-free sustainability.
